title: Dividing by a Multiple of Ten

steps.body: A divisor that is a multiple of ten splits into two easy steps: dividing by 30 is dividing by 3 and then by 10.
steps.narration: A divisor that is a multiple of ten splits into two easy steps: dividing by 30 is dividing by 3 and then by 10.

widget.prompt: How many 30s fit in 240? Hop by thirties.

commonLandings.feedback: Seven hops reach 210; one more thirty still fits inside 240.
Nine hops overshoot 240 — eight is the exact count.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 430, 3 hops land on 460.
widget.successFeedback: 240 after eight hops — so 240 ÷ 30 = 8, found by counting groups of thirty.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — eight hops of thirty are needed to reach 240.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — eight hops of thirty stop exactly on 240.

predict.prompt: Is dividing by 30 easier than by 27?
predict.reveal: A multiple of ten splits into a familiar fact and a place-value shift; 27 offers no such split.

cml.actionGoal: Count how many whole groups of the divisor fit, in whatever batches are convenient, for g5ld mult ten.
invariants: Division counts groups, and every method — estimating, partial quotients, the standard algorithm — counts the SAME groups in different batches, which is why g5ld mult ten always ends with quotient times divisor plus remainder rebuilding the dividend.
misconceptions: Placing a quotient digit a place out, treating an overshoot as final rather than adjusting the trial digit, or reporting a remainder that is as large as the divisor.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the remainder came out equal to the divisor, what would that tell you about the quotient?

widget.prompt: Why is dividing by 30 easier than dividing by 27?

options.label: Because 30 is 3 × 10
options.feedback: Correct — a multiple of ten splits into a familiar fact and a place-value shift.

options.label: Because 30 is larger
options.feedback: Size is not the reason; dividing by 33 is no easier than by 27 despite being larger.

options.label: Because 27 is odd
options.feedback: Parity does not matter — dividing by 26 is no easier than dividing by 27.

options.label: They are equally easy
options.feedback: The place-value shortcut is only available when the divisor is a multiple of ten.

hints: Divide by the digit, then by ten.

widget.prompt: Compute 340 ÷ 20 — dividing by a multiple of ten.

commonErrors.feedback: That divided by 2 rather than 20; the extra zero is a whole place value.
That divided by ten alone, leaving the 2 in the divisor unused.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Ask how many whole groups of the divisor the dividend holds, then check what is left over.

commonErrors.feedback: That misplaced the quotient's digits by a whole place; check how many groups the first partial step accounts for.
Subtracting the divisor once removes a single group; division counts how many groups FIT.
